claims.summary: On a finite set with a stochastic splitting rule P, irreducible and reversible with respect to pi (conductances c(x,y) = pi(x)p(x,y)), and initial mass eta and thresholds t with equal sums: every divisible-sandpile odometer v >= 0 whose final configuration eta - v + P^T v is at most t ends exactly at t, and its net flow v(x)p(x,y) - v(y)p(y,x) equals c(x,y)(u(x) - u(y)) for any solution of sum_y c(x,y)(u(x) - u(y)) = eta(x) - t(x): the same for every such stabilizing odometer, linear in eta - t, the electrical (least-energy) flow; odometers exist (v = pi (u - min u)). For a non-reversible rule the flow is unique only up to a circulation. With equal splitting on the grid of cells and uniform thresholds, the sandpile odometer flow is the electrical flow, and every balanced transport flow is it plus a divergence-free circulation.
claims.assessment: Working proof: the stochastic rule conserves mass, so a stable configuration with the thresholds' total equals them; reversibility turns the balance equation into a weighted Laplacian equation, whose kernel on an irreducible chain is the constants; Thomson's principle by orthogonality to divergence-free flows.
claims.rationale: Decides the premise of the queued sandpile-odometer-flow item: in the balanced setting on the square the odometer flow is the electrical flow, a fixed linear kernel, for which the fourth route review's Holtsmark sketch predicts Gaussian per-point tails; nonlinearity needs slack or a state-dependent rule, whose flows are the electrical flow plus a circulation.
claims.next_action: Test whether the circulation of the state-dependent sandpile (mass sent only to neighbours below threshold) lightens the per-point tails of the electrical flow on the grid.
